metadata.title: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
metadata.description:
For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n at least 2, an explicit nonnegative singleton-supported cycle rank q_n is subtracted from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound. The correction depends only on the two preceding incidence ranks. Terminal-preserving witness trees prove the cycle transfer b_n at least q_n. Standard reflected Young-prefix examples attain strict improvements from 31 to 30 for r=3 and from 20 to 19 for r=1, making coefficient one sharp. A singleton-successor sufficient condition, conditional two-witness equality characterization and the all-r rank-three consequence are proved.

This answers Majumder's printed request for an improvement of the Byrnes inequality in an incidence-dependent form. Stanley's general local recurrence, the separate combinatorial strict-growth-proof question and improvement of the global Fibonacci envelope are not claimed. Classical incidence identities, graph facts, singleton methods and Wagner reflection are credited. Gaetz-Venkataramana Proposition 3.4 already gives the exact rank-one two-singleton lemma used in the rank-three deduction; the witness poset families are standard. A dated bounded primary-source comparison found no earlier equivalent supported-cycle upper-bound theorem in inspected material; historical firstness, a new general method and present worldwide openness are not certified.

The deposit consists of a seven-page paper and a complete editable-source/verification ZIP, preserving all eight original submitted artifacts. Portable standard-library exact checks, complete expected outputs, closed manifests and a local rebuild script are included. Finite computations supplement the written universal proof and do not certify full recurrence or literature absence. AI tools were extensively involved in research planning, mathematical exploration and proof development/reconstruction, computation, source and literature investigation, writing, editing and adversarial verification. Alec Kriebel is the named human author. This work is unrefereed, without professional independent human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification; internal AI reviews do not supply those certifications.
